thread_analysis.thread_summary: This is an internal Allion exchange (December 3-8, 2025) tracking Profile testing progress for [COMPANY]'s 19AVNJ product. Initial testing showed about 90% PASS, with several FAIL items to investigate. The team resolves a question about a non-mandatory (Category D) A2DP test case missing from PTS, identifies the cause of an AVRCP/CT/MCN/CB metadata test failure (insufficient metadata size to trigger fragmentation), escalates unresolved OPP test failures to the customer for guidance on test sample operation, and finally addresses a remaining AVRCP cover-art test failure via a PTS configuration parameter rather than escalating a basic question to the BQTF.
all_questions_found: Is the A2DP/SNK/SYN test case, which is missing from PTS and falls under Test Case Category D, acceptable to leave un-executed?
Why does the AVRCP/CT/MCN/CB test case result in FAIL, and how can it be made to pass?
Several OPP test cases (SRM, SRMP, BCE, BCP, GOEP/BC) failed - what should be done to resolve or escalate these failures?
Should the team ask the BQTF a general question about how to run the AVRCP cover-art test, or is there a PTS parameter that resolves the remaining failure?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Profile testing for 19AVNJ covered A2DP, AVRCP, and OPP. A2DP/SNK/SYN was unavailable in PTS but is Category D (non-mandatory), so it was excluded as out of scope. AVRCP/CT/MCN/CB failed because the test music file's metadata was below the 512KB threshold needed to trigger response fragmentation - resolved by using a music file with larger metadata. Multiple OPP test cases (GOEP/SRM, SRMP, BCE, BCP, GOEP/BC) failed and, since the cause wasn't clear from logs, were escalated to the customer with PTS report and TeraTerm logs requesting guidance on test sample operation. After re-testing, all cases passed except AVRCP/CT/MCN/CB, which was finally addressed via the PTS parameter TSPX_no_cover_art_folder (a virtual file system path for media without cover art, used by cover art test cases) rather than escalating to the BQTF.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Each FAIL item was triaged by first checking whether it was even in scope (Category D / not in PTS -> exclude), then determining whether the failure was due to test setup/configuration (metadata size threshold, PTS PIXIT parameters) versus a genuine device behavior issue requiring customer input (OPP test sample operation). The team explicitly preferred resolving issues via correct PTS/PIXIT configuration over escalating procedural questions to the BQTF.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly excluding a mandatory test case as 'Category D/not in PTS' could leave required testing undone. Failing to recognize the metadata-size requirement for AVRCP/CT/MCN/CB could result in repeated, unresolvable FAILs being misattributed to the device. Not escalating unresolved OPP failures to the customer for DUT operation guidance could waste testing cycles. Escalating basic PTS configuration questions to the BQTF instead of resolving them via PIXIT parameters wastes the BQTF's time and could affect the working relationship.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When triaging Profile test FAILs: first confirm whether the failing test case is actually in scope (check ICS category and PTS availability); for metadata-related AVRCP failures, check the test file's metadata size against documented thresholds (e.g., 512KB for fragmentation); for failures that seem related to DUT operation, escalate to the customer with full logs (PTS report + TeraTerm) rather than guessing; and always check PTS/PIXIT configuration parameters (e.g., TSPX_no_cover_art_folder) before raising procedural questions with the BQTF.
